Parameter: Drift Threshold (Trigger); Setting: 5% relative drift from target allocation at asset class level; Rationale: Balances transaction costs against tracking error; 5% is industry standard for balanced portfolios; Override Conditions: Manual override for accounts with >$50K tax impact; ti…
tool:ch3:s3.4-3-4-rebalancing-engine-con.raw_text:
Orion Trading's rebalancing engine is configured with Meridian-specific rules that govern when and how portfolios are rebalanced, incorporating tax awareness, cash management, and compliance constraints.
Parameter: Drift Threshold (Trigger); Setting: 5% relative drift from target allocation at asset class level; Rationale: Balances transaction costs against tracking error; 5% is industry standard for balanced portfolios; Override Conditions: Manual override for accounts with >$50K tax impact; tighter 3% threshold for institutional accounts
Parameter: Minimum Trade Size; Setting: $500 per security per account; Rationale: Avoids uneconomic small trades; reduces custodian ticket charges; Override Conditions: Waived for complete liquidations, tax-loss harvesting, or model changes
Parameter: Tax-Loss Harvesting Mode; Setting: Enabled for all taxable accounts; $1,000 minimum loss threshold; Rationale: Systematic TLH across all eligible accounts; losses offset gains and up to $3,000 ordinary income; Override Conditions: Disabled for accounts with wash-sale risk from held-away accounts; disabled during December wash-sale window (Dec 1–31 for sales, Jan 1–30 for repurchases)
Parameter: Wash-Sale Prevention; Setting: 30-day hold on repurchasing substantially identical securities across all accounts in household; Rationale: IRS wash-sale rule compliance across all custodians and account types; Override Conditions: No override permitted — hard compliance rule
Parameter: Cash Buffer; Setting: 2% cash target for taxable accounts; 1% for retirement accounts; Rationale: Ensures sufficient cash for fee billing, distributions, and management fees without forced liquidation; Override Conditions: Higher cash buffers for accounts with known upcoming distributions; zero cash for fully invested strategies
Parameter: Realized Gain Budget; Setting: Annual realized gain limit per account set collaboratively with client (default: $0 for taxable accounts unless client approves); Rationale: Prevents unexpected tax bills; aligns trading activity with client's tax situation and expectations; Override Conditions: Unlimited gain budget for tax-exempt accounts (IRAs, Roth); overridden by model changes or client-directed liquidations
Parameter: Restricted Security List; Setting: SEC-restricted list (employee trading); client-specific restrictions (ESG exclusions, employer stock limitations); Rationale: Legal compliance for employee personal trading; alignment with client values and employment restrictions; Override Conditions: Updated monthly by compliance; client-specific restrictions updated at onboarding and annual review
Parameter: Block Trade Allocation; Setting: Pro-rata allocation based on account order size; partial fills distributed proportionally; Rationale: Fair allocation across all accounts per SEC/FINRA guidance; no preferential allocation; Override Conditions: No override — regulatory requirement
Parameter: Rebalancing Frequency; Setting: Continuous monitoring with quarterly full rebalance; event-driven rebalancing for cash flows >$25,000; Rationale: Combines systematic discipline with responsiveness to significant cash movements; Override Conditions: Immediate rebalancing for new accounts, model changes, or Investment Committee tactical shifts
Table 3.4: Rebalancing Engine Configuration Parameters

tool:ch4.content_summary: Chapter 4: Financial Planning & Advisory Software Suite
tool:ch4.raw_text: Meridian's financial planning technology stack enables advisors to deliver comprehensive, personalized financial plans covering retirement, tax, estate, education, insurance, and cash flow analysis. This chapter documents every planning tool, its configuration, integration points, and operational procedures.

Feature: Balance Sheet / Net Worth; Configuration / Usage at Meridian…
tool:ch4:s4.1-4-1-primary-planning-tool-.raw_text:
Feature: Client Fact Finder; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Digital questionnaire sent to clients pre-meeting; captures income, expenses, assets, liabilities, insurance, estate documents, goals; Data Source: Client input (emailed link) → advisor review and validation → sync to Salesforce; Output: Populated eMoney client record; PDF summary for file; User Access: All 30 planners; clients have self-service fact finder access
Feature: Balance Sheet / Net Worth; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Real-time aggregation of custodial accounts (via Orion feed) + held-away accounts (Yodlee aggregation) + manual entries (real estate, business interests, collectibles); Data Source: Orion API (custodial); Yodlee (held-away); manual entry (real estate appraisals, business valuations); Output: Consolidated net worth statement; trend analysis; asset allocation pie chart; User Access: Advisor and client portal
Feature: Cash Flow Analysis; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Monthly income vs. expense modeling with inflation adjustments; tracks discretionary vs. non-discretionary spending; integrates Yodlee transaction categorization; Data Source: Yodlee transaction feed; client-reported budget; tax return data (manual entry); Output: Annual cash flow projection; savings rate calculation; surplus/deficit identification; User Access: Planners
Feature: Monte Carlo Simulation; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: 1,000 iterations; uses Capital Market Assumptions updated annually by Investment Committee; adjustable confidence interval display (typically 75–90%); Data Source: Meridian CMA (expected returns, std dev, correlations by asset class); client portfolio allocation; withdrawal plan; Output: Probability of success for each goal; distribution of outcomes; sensitivity analysis; User Access: Planners; results shared with clients in review meetings
Feature: Retirement Analysis; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Multi-scenario modeling: early/on-time/delayed retirement; Social Security optimization (break-even, spousal, survivor); Roth conversion analysis; RMD projections; Medicare/IRMAA modeling; Data Source: Client income history; Social Security statement (uploaded or estimated); pension details; healthcare cost assumptions (Fidelity data); tax bracket projections; Output: Year-by-year retirement income projection; Social Security claiming recommendation; Roth conversion schedule; tax bracket map through retirement; User Access: Planners
Feature: Estate Planning Module; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Current estate map; trust flow visualization; estate tax projection (federal + state); asset titling analysis; beneficiary review; Data Source: Client estate documents (will, trusts, POA) → manual entry of provisions; account titling from Orion; beneficiary designations from custodians; Output: Estate settlement projection; estate tax liability estimate; flow-of-assets diagram; recommended titling changes; User Access: Planners with estate planning credential (CFP, AEP, CTFA)
Feature: Tax Planning Module; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Current year tax projection; multi-year tax bracket analysis; Roth conversion optimization; charitable giving strategy modeling; capital gain/loss harvesting coordination; Data Source: Prior year tax return (client upload); Orion realized gains/losses; estimated income data; charitable giving history; Output: Projected tax liability; Roth conversion opportunity windows; TLH opportunity identification; bracket management strategy; User Access: Planners
Feature: Insurance Analysis; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Life insurance needs analysis (income replacement, debt payoff, education funding, estate liquidity); disability income gap analysis; LTC cost modeling; Data Source: Client income data; existing policies (manual entry); expense data; goal data; Output: Insurance gap identification; coverage recommendation; premium comparison (referral to insurance specialist); User Access: Planners
Feature: Education Planning; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: 529 plan modeling; financial aid optimization (FAFSA/CSS Profile impact); cost projections with inflation (College Board data); Data Source: Child ages; target schools; current 529 balances; parent income/assets for aid eligibility; Output: Savings recommendation; 529 contribution schedule; financial aid eligibility estimate; User Access: Planners
Feature: Client Vault; Configuration / Usage at Meridian: Secure document storage accessible by client and advisor; organized by category (tax, estate, insurance, statements, correspondence); Data Source: Client uploads; advisor uploads; automated statement delivery from custodians (via Orion integration); Output: Organized, searchable document repository; expiration tracking for time-sensitive documents; User Access: Clients + advisors; permission-controlled access

tool:ch4:s4.3-4-3-risk-assessment-riskal.raw_text:
Riskalyze (rebranded as Nitrogen Wealth) provides quantified risk tolerance assessment and portfolio risk analysis. Every new client completes a Riskalyze questionnaire during onboarding, and existing clients are re-assessed annually or when significant life events occur.
Component: Risk Number Questionnaire; How It Works at Meridian: 6-question behavioral finance questionnaire measuring comfort with hypothetical portfolio gains and losses over 6-month period; generates 'Risk Number' on 1–99 scale; Output: Client Risk Number (e.g., 62); risk range (e.g., comfortable with portfolios scored 52–72); risk capacity assessment; Integration: Risk Number syncs to Salesforce via API → used in suitability documentation → compared to portfolio actual risk score nightly
Component: Portfolio Risk Analysis; How It Works at Meridian: Uploads current portfolio holdings; calculates portfolio Risk Number based on historical volatility, correlations, and 95% confidence interval; Output: Portfolio Risk Number; 95% downside/upside range over 6 months; position-level risk contribution; sector/factor concentration analysis; Integration: Orion holdings → Riskalyze analysis → risk mismatch alerts if portfolio risk deviates >20% from client Risk Number
Component: Stress Testing; How It Works at Meridian: Pre-built and custom stress scenarios: 2008 Financial Crisis, 2020 COVID, Rising Rate (+300bps), Inflation Shock, Sector Collapse; Output: Projected portfolio impact under each scenario; comparison to client risk tolerance; identification of vulnerable positions; Integration: Results stored in Riskalyze; PDF reports generated for client review meetings; scenario results linked to Salesforce
Component: Proposal Generation; How It Works at Meridian: Side-by-side comparison of current portfolio vs. proposed Meridian model portfolio; shows risk improvement and fee comparison; Output: Branded PDF proposal showing: current vs. proposed Risk Number, expected range of outcomes, fee comparison, transition tax cost estimate; Integration: Proposals linked to Salesforce Opportunity; used in prospect conversion meetings
Component: Compliance Documentation; How It Works at Meridian: Automated documentation of risk assessment at onboarding and each annual review; captures questionnaire responses, risk number, portfolio alignment; Output: Compliance-ready PDF: timestamped risk assessment, signed acknowledgment (DocuSign integration), portfolio alignment verification; Integration: Archived in Smarsh (email) and Salesforce (document attachment); available for SEC/FINRA examination

tool:ch5.heading: Chapter 5: Compliance, Regulatory & Surveillance Tools
tool:ch5.raw_text: Compliance technology is not optional—it is a regulatory necessity. SEC and FINRA examinations routinely evaluate the adequacy of compliance systems, surveillance tools, and documentation practices. This chapter documents every compliance tool in Meridian's arsenal, its configuration, the regulatory requirement it satisfies, and the procedures for its use.
tool:ch5.label: Chapter 5: Compliance, Regulatory & Surveillance Tools

Tool: MyComplianceOffice; Vendor: MCO; Primary Function: Compliance workflow management: employee personal trading, gifts & entertainment, outside business activities, political contributions, code of ethics attestation; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC Rule 204A-1 (Code of Ethics); Rule 204-2 (Books & Records); FINRA Rules 3110, 3210, 3280; Users: CCO + 3 compliance staff; all employees (self-reporting); Annual Cost: $36,000; Integration: Schwab/Fidelity personal account feeds; Azure AD for employee roster
Tool: Smarsh Connected Archive; Vendor: Smarsh; Primary Function: Unified communications archiving: email, text messages (via Smarsh Capture), Teams messages, social media, website content; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC Rule 204-2(a)(7) (correspondence retention); FINRA Rules 3110.09, 4511, 2210; SEC Marketing Rule; Users: CCO + compliance; all communications auto-captured; Annual Cost: $48,000; Integration: Microsoft 365 (email/Teams); Twilio (SMS); LinkedIn; firm website
Tool: Global Relay (backup archive); Vendor: Global Relay; Primary Function: Secondary email archive for redundancy; WORM-compliant storage; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC Rule 17a-4 (WORM storage requirement for broker-dealer records); prudent practice for RIAs; Users: CCO; Annual Cost: $12,000; Integration: Microsoft 365 email journal
Tool: Orion Compliance Module; Vendor: Orion; Primary Function: Pre-trade and post-trade compliance checking; investment policy monitoring; restricted list enforcement; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC Rule 206(4)-7 (Compliance Program); Reg BI Best Interest obligation; fiduciary duty; Users: Traders, PMs, compliance staff; Annual Cost: Included in Orion license; Integration: Orion Trading (pre-trade); Orion Connect (post-trade monitoring)
Tool: Riskalyze (Nitrogen) Compliance; Vendor: Nitrogen; Primary Function: Suitability documentation; risk tolerance assessment; portfolio-client alignment monitoring; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC/FINRA suitability and best interest requirements; Reg BI documentation; Users: All advisors + compliance; Annual Cost: Included in Riskalyze license; Integration: Salesforce (risk scores); Orion (portfolio alignment)
Tool: RIA in a Box (MyRIACompliance); Vendor: RIA in a Box; Primary Function: Regulatory filing management: Form ADV, Form CRS, state registrations, annual compliance calendar, mock audit preparation; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC Registration (Form ADV Parts 1, 2A, 2B, CRS); state notice filings; annual updating amendment; Users: CCO + operations director; Annual Cost: $8,400; Integration: SEC IARD system; state regulators
Tool: AML/KYC Platform (Custom); Vendor: Internal (built on Salesforce); Primary Function: Client identity verification, OFAC screening, PEP screening, SAR filing workflow, CIP documentation; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: Bank Secrecy Act; USA PATRIOT Act; FinCEN requirements (applicable to certain RIAs; prudent practice for all); Users: Operations + compliance; Annual Cost: Internal development cost; Integration: OFAC SDN list (daily download); World-Check (Refinitiv); Salesforce Cases
Tool: Compliance Calendar (Custom); Vendor: Internal (Salesforce + Outlook); Primary Function: Master calendar of all compliance deadlines: ADV amendments, state filings, annual review, testing schedules, board meetings; Regulatory Requirement Addressed: SEC Rule 206(4)-7 (annual review requirement); all regulatory filing deadlines; Users: CCO; automated reminders to responsible parties; Annual Cost: N/A (internal); Integration: Salesforce Tasks; Outlook calendar invites; Slack reminders

tool:ch5:s5.2-5-2-email-communications-s.heading: 5.2 Email & Communications Surveillance
tool:ch5:s5.2-5-2-email-communications-s.content_summary:
Smarsh captures and archives approximately 15,000 emails per month, 2,000 Teams messages, and 500 text messages across Meridian's operations. The surveillance system applies lexicon-based screening and AI-assisted review to identify potential compliance violations.
Surveillance Category: Client Complaints; Lexicon / Detection Rules: Keywords indicating dissatisfaction, loss, litigation, regulatory inquiry; Sample Trigger Terms: 'complaint', 'sue', 'lawyer', 'FINRA', 'SEC', 'lost money', 'unautho…
tool:ch5:s5.2-5-2-email-communications-s.raw_text:
Smarsh captures and archives approximately 15,000 emails per month, 2,000 Teams messages, and 500 text messages across Meridian's operations. The surveillance system applies lexicon-based screening and AI-assisted review to identify potential compliance violations.
Surveillance Category: Client Complaints; Lexicon / Detection Rules: Keywords indicating dissatisfaction, loss, litigation, regulatory inquiry; Sample Trigger Terms: 'complaint', 'sue', 'lawyer', 'FINRA', 'SEC', 'lost money', 'unauthorized', 'misled', 'unsuitable', 'fiduciary breach'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~25 alerts; Review SLA: 24-hour review; Escalation Path: CCO → Managing Principal → outside counsel if warranted
Surveillance Category: Insider Trading / MNPI; Lexicon / Detection Rules: References to material non-public information, tips, advance knowledge; Sample Trigger Terms: 'insider', 'not public', 'announcement tomorrow', 'merger', 'acquisition target', 'earnings leak', 'before the news'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~15 alerts; Review SLA: Same-day review; Escalation Path: CCO → securities counsel → SEC/FINRA reporting if substantiated
Surveillance Category: Gifts & Entertainment; Lexicon / Detection Rules: Offers of gifts, meals, entertainment that may exceed policy limits ($250/gift, $500/event); Sample Trigger Terms: 'tickets', 'dinner', 'golf', 'trip', 'gift', 'thank you for the [item]', 'box seats', 'concert'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~40 alerts; Review SLA: 48-hour review; Escalation Path: CCO → disclosure to MyComplianceOffice; pre-clearance required >$100
Surveillance Category: Outside Business Activities; Lexicon / Detection Rules: References to employment, board service, or business outside Meridian; Sample Trigger Terms: 'consulting', 'my other business', 'board member', 'side project', 'moonlighting', 'LLC', 'my company'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~10 alerts; Review SLA: 48-hour review; Escalation Path: CCO → employee interview → MyComplianceOffice OBA disclosure
Surveillance Category: Marketing / Advertising; Lexicon / Detection Rules: Unapproved testimonials, performance claims, misleading statements; Sample Trigger Terms: 'guaranteed', 'no risk', 'always', 'never lose', 'best returns', 'outperform', client testimonial without disclaimer; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~20 alerts; Review SLA: 48-hour review; Escalation Path: CCO → marketing review → correction/retraction if needed
Surveillance Category: Elder Financial Exploitation; Lexicon / Detection Rules: Patterns suggesting exploitation of elderly or vulnerable clients; Sample Trigger Terms: 'power of attorney', 'confused', 'doesn't understand', 'caregiver says', 'new friend', 'large withdrawal', 'changed beneficiary'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~8 alerts; Review SLA: Same-day review; Escalation Path: CCO → APS reporting if substantiated; temporary hold per state law
Surveillance Category: Private Securities Transactions; Lexicon / Detection Rules: References to selling away, private placements outside firm; Sample Trigger Terms: 'private deal', 'invest with me personally', 'off the books', 'promissory note', 'my fund'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~5 alerts; Review SLA: Same-day review; Escalation Path: CCO → immediate investigation; potential termination and regulatory reporting
Surveillance Category: Political Contributions; Lexicon / Detection Rules: References to political donations that may trigger SEC pay-to-play rules; Sample Trigger Terms: 'campaign', 'donate', 'contribution', 'fundraiser', 'political', 'PAC', 'candidate'; Alert Volume (Monthly): ~12 alerts; Review SLA: 72-hour review; Escalation Path: CCO → MyComplianceOffice; Rule 206(4)-5 analysis

tool:ch6.heading: Chapter 6: Document Management System & PDF Document Library
tool:ch6.content_summary: Chapter 6: Document Management System & PDF Document Library
tool:ch6.raw_text: Meridian generates, receives, stores, and retrieves over 150,000 documents annually across client service, compliance, operations, and investment management functions. This chapter catalogs every document type, its storage location, retention period, access controls, and the systems used to manage the document lifecycle.
tool:ch6.label: Chapter 6: Document Management System & PDF Document Library

tool:ch6:s6.1-6-1-document-management-ar.heading: 6.1 Document Management Architecture
tool:ch6:s6.1-6-1-document-management-ar.content_summary:
Meridian's document management follows a three-tier architecture: active working documents in SharePoint Online, client-facing documents in eMoney Vault/Salesforce, and long-term compliance archives in Smarsh/S3 Glacier.

tool:ch6:s6.2.1-client-onboarding-docume.content_summary: Document Name: Investment Management Agreement (IMA); Purpose: Master agreement authorizing Meridian to manage client assets on a discretionary basis; defines scope of services, fee schedule, termination provisions; Pages (Typical): 12–18; Template Location: SharePoint: /Templates/Onboarding/IMA_v4.2.docx; Generation Method: Mail merge from Salesforce client data → DocuSign envelope; Signature Required: Yes (DocuSign eSignature — all parties); Retention: Permanent (duration of relationship + 7 y…
tool:ch6:s6.2.1-client-onboarding-docume.raw_text:
Document Name: Investment Management Agreement (IMA); Purpose: Master agreement authorizing Meridian to manage client assets on a discretionary basis; defines scope of services, fee schedule, termination provisions; Pages (Typical): 12–18; Template Location: SharePoint: /Templates/Onboarding/IMA_v4.2.docx; Generation Method: Mail merge from Salesforce client data → DocuSign envelope; Signature Required: Yes (DocuSign eSignature — all parties); Retention: Permanent (duration of relationship + 7 years); Regulatory Basis: SEC Rule 204-3; Investment Advisers Act Section 205
Document Name: Investment Policy Statement (IPS); Purpose: Documents client's investment objectives, risk tolerance, time horizon, constraints, and agreed-upon asset allocation; basis for all investment decisions; Pages (Typical): 8–12; Template Location: SharePoint: /Templates/Onboarding/IPS_v3.8.docx; Generation Method: Generated from Riskalyze risk assessment + eMoney plan data → advisor customization → DocuSign; Signature Required: Yes (client + advisor); Retention: Duration of relationship + 7 years; updated annually; Regulatory Basis: SEC fiduciary duty documentation; Reg BI best interest basis
Document Name: Form ADV Part 2A Brochure; Purpose: Firm brochure describing services, fees, conflicts of interest, disciplinary history, financial condition; Pages (Typical): 35–40; Template Location: SharePoint: /Compliance/ADV/Part2A_Current.pdf; Generation Method: Prepared by RIA in a Box; filed via IARD; PDF distributed to clients; Signature Required: Client acknowledgment of receipt (DocuSign); Retention: Permanent; Regulatory Basis: SEC Rule 204-3(a); Form ADV instructions
Document Name: Form ADV Part 2B Brochure Supplement; Purpose: Individual advisor supplement with education, business experience, disciplinary information, outside business activities; Pages (Typical): 2–4 per advisor; Template Location: SharePoint: /Compliance/ADV/Part2B/[AdvisorName].pdf; Generation Method: Prepared by compliance; filed via IARD; Signature Required: Client acknowledgment of receipt; Retention: Permanent; Regulatory Basis: SEC Rule 204-3(b)
Document Name: Form CRS (Client Relationship Summary); Purpose: Plain-language summary of services, fees, conflicts, standards of conduct, disciplinary history; Pages (Typical): 2 (SEC-mandated maximum); Template Location: SharePoint: /Compliance/CRS/FormCRS_Current.pdf; Generation Method: Prepared by compliance per SEC format requirements; Signature Required: Client acknowledgment of receipt; Retention: Permanent; Regulatory Basis: SEC Reg BI; Form CRS instructions
Document Name: Privacy Notice (Regulation S-P); Purpose: Notice of firm's privacy practices regarding collection, sharing, and protection of client personal information; Pages (Typical): 2–3; Template Location: SharePoint: /Compliance/Privacy/PrivacyNotice_v2.pdf; Generation Method: Annual distribution via eMoney Vault and email; Signature Required: No signature; delivery tracked in Salesforce; Retention: Permanent; Regulatory Basis: SEC Regulation S-P; Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act
Document Name: Account Application / New Account Form; Purpose: Custodian-specific account opening paperwork capturing account type, owner information, beneficiaries, funding method; Pages (Typical): 4–8 (varies by custodian and account type); Template Location: Custodian portals: Schwab Advisor Center / Fidelity WealthScape / Pershing NetExchange; Generation Method: Custodian online application prepopulated from Salesforce data → DocuSign for signature → submitted to custodian; Signature Required: Yes (all account holders); Retention: 7 years post-account-closure; Regulatory Basis: SEC Rule 204-2(a)(14); custodian requirements
Document Name: ACATS Transfer Form; Purpose: Authorization to transfer assets from prior custodian to Meridian's custodian via Automated Customer Account Transfer Service; Pages (Typical): 1–2; Template Location: Custodian portals; Generation Method: Custodian-specific electronic ACATS initiation; Signature Required: Yes (account holder); Retention: 7 years; Regulatory Basis: FINRA Rule 11870; ACATS Operating Procedures
Document Name: Beneficiary Designation Form; Purpose: Names primary and contingent beneficiaries for retirement accounts, insurance, TOD registrations; Pages (Typical): 1–2; Template Location: Custodian portals + internal template for non-custodial accounts; Generation Method: Custodian online form or internal PDF template → DocuSign; Signature Required: Yes (account holder); Retention: Permanent (until superseded; retain all prior versions); Regulatory Basis: ERISA (retirement accounts); state law; custodian requirements
Document Name: W-9 / W-8BEN Tax Certification; Purpose: IRS form certifying taxpayer identification number and tax status; W-8BEN for non-US persons; Pages (Typical): 1–2; Template Location: IRS.gov / custodian portals; Generation Method: IRS form completed by client; submitted to custodian with account application; Signature Required: Yes (taxpayer); Retention: Duration of account + 7 years; Regulatory Basis: IRS Sec. 3406 (backup withholding); FATCA

Document Name: Quarterly Performance Report; Purpose: Comprehensive portfolio performance report showing TWR, MWR, benchmark comparison, asset allocation, holdings, transaction summary, and market commentary; Frequency: Quarterly; Generation System: Orion Connect → Tamarac Reporting (custom template) → PDF generation; Delivery Method: eMoney Vault + client portal + optional email delivery; Pages: 8–15 per household; Retention: 7 years
Document Name: Annual Investment Review Presentation; Purpose: Year-in-review document covering annual performance, market recap, portfolio changes, look-ahead, planning updates; Frequency: Annual; Generation System: PowerPoint template populated with Orion data + CIO commentary → PDF; Delivery Method: Presented in annual review meeting; PDF filed in Salesforce; Pages: 15–25 slides; Retention: 7 years

Document Name: Tax Reporting Package; Purpose: Consolidated 1099 summary, realized gain/loss report, tax lot detail, cost basis reconciliation, K-1 summaries (if applicable); Frequency: Annual (January–March); Generation System: Orion tax reporting module + custodian 1099 data → custom Excel/PDF package; Delivery Method: eMoney Vault + email to client's CPA (with client authorization); Pages: 10–30 per household; Retention: 7 years
Document Name: Fee Invoice / Billing Summary; Purpose: Detailed fee calculation showing AUM tiers, fee rate, billing period, account-level charges, any fee offsets or credits; Frequency: Quarterly; Generation System: Orion Billing → PDF invoice → Salesforce attachment; Delivery Method: eMoney Vault; email notification to client; custodian debit authorization; Pages: 1–3 per billing group; Retention: 7 years
Document Name: Financial Plan Summary Report; Purpose: Condensed version of comprehensive financial plan showing goals, probability of success, key recommendations, action items; Frequency: As plans are created/updated (typically annually); Generation System: eMoney export → PDF; RightCapital export → PDF; Delivery Method: Presented in planning meeting; PDF filed in eMoney Vault and Salesforce; Pages: 20–40; Retention: 7 years post-plan-expiry
Document Name: Portfolio Rebalancing Report; Purpose: Documents each rebalancing event: before/after allocation, trades executed, tax impact, rationale; Frequency: Per rebalancing event (quarterly + event-driven); Generation System: Orion Trading → rebalancing summary report → PDF; Delivery Method: Filed in Salesforce; available on client portal for discretionary accounts; Pages: 2–5 per event; Retention: 7 years
Document Name: Consolidated Net Worth Statement; Purpose: Aggregated view of all client assets (custodial + held-away + real estate + business interests + insurance cash values) and liabilities; Frequency: Quarterly or semi-annually; Generation System: eMoney aggregation → PDF export; Delivery Method: eMoney Vault + review meeting; Pages: 3–6; Retention: 7 years

tool:ch7.heading: Chapter 7: Market Data, Research Databases & Data Feeds
tool:ch7.content_summary: Chapter 7: Market Data, Research Databases & Data Feeds
tool:ch7.raw_text: Meridian Wealth Advisors relies on a sophisticated ecosystem of market data vendors, research databases, and real-time data feeds to power investment research, portfolio analysis, compliance reporting, and client communication. This chapter details the complete data infrastructure, including Bloomberg, Refinitiv, FactSet, and alternative data providers, along with integration architecture and data quality procedures that ensure portfolio decisions are based on accurate, timely information.
tool:ch7.label: Chapter 7: Market Data, Research Databases & Data Feeds

tool:ch7:s7.1-7-1-real-time-market-data-.content_summary:

Meridian integrates multiple vendors to ensure redundancy and comprehensive coverage across asset classes. Each feed includes custom configuration for data priority, validation rules, and failover behavior.

tool:ch7:s7.4-7-4-data-quality-validatio.raw_text:
Data quality is mission-critical. Meridian operates a multi-layered validation framework that reconciles pricing across vendors, detects outliers, and flags data anomalies in real time. Daily reconciliation reports compare key indices and asset classes across all feeds to identify discrepancies before they impact portfolios.
Key procedures include:
- Automated daily reconciliation: Compare closing prices for all holdings against Bloomberg reference data; flag discrepancies >0.5%
- Corporate action monitoring: Validate splits, dividends, and distributions across vendors within 1 business day of occurrence
- FX rate reconciliation: Cross-check daily FX rates against 3+ sources; use median when variance exceeds thresholds
- Performance attribution audit: Reconcile monthly and quarterly performance calculations across Tamarac and Orion systems
- Index rebalance tracking: Monitor quarterly rebalances for target indices; validate constituent changes within 24 hours
- Manual review threshold: Any data anomaly >2 standard deviations triggers escalation to Chief Investment Officer
Validation Rule: Price outlier detection; Data Types Monitored: All equity, bond prices; Check Frequency: Real-time / EOD; Tolerance Threshold: >5% move without news; Escalation Path: Compliance Officer; Owner: Operations
Validation Rule: Corporate action validation; Data Types Monitored: Dividends, splits, distributions; Check Frequency: Daily; Tolerance Threshold: Same-day publication; Escalation Path: Chief Investment Officer; Owner: Research
Validation Rule: FX rate reconciliation; Data Types Monitored: All currency pairs; Check Frequency: EOD; Tolerance Threshold: >0.1% variance from median; Escalation Path: Treasury; Owner: Operations
Validation Rule: Fund NAV verification; Data Types Monitored: All mutual fund prices; Check Frequency: EOD; Tolerance Threshold: ±$0.01 variance; Escalation Path: Fund Admin; Owner: Operations
Validation Rule: Index constituent validation; Data Types Monitored: S&P 500, Russell 2000, custom indices; Check Frequency: EOQ; Tolerance Threshold: Timely constituent changes; Escalation Path: Chief Investment Officer; Owner: Research
Validation Rule: Performance calculation audit; Data Types Monitored: Time-weighted and money-weighted returns; Check Frequency: Monthly; Tolerance Threshold: Within 0.01% of Orion baseline; Escalation Path: Controller; Owner: Accounting
Table 7.4: Data Quality and Reconciliation Procedures

tool:ch8:s8.4-8-4-data-warehouse-and-etl.raw_text:
Meridian operates a cloud-based data warehouse on Azure Synapse that consolidates data from Orion, Tamarac, Salesforce, accounting systems, and market data feeds. The warehouse enables complex analytics, historical trending, and regulatory reporting that would be difficult within source systems alone.
▌ KEY INSIGHT: The data warehouse is the single source of truth for firm-wide metrics; all dashboards and reports query this system to ensure consistency.
ETL pipelines are orchestrated via Azure Data Factory with 150+ scheduled jobs running on hourly to daily cadence. Pipelines include data validation, deduplication, and transformation into star schema design optimized for reporting and analysis.
- Orion Portfolio Data Pipeline: Hourly extraction of positions, trades, cash, performance; transformation into fact and dimension tables
- Tamarac Client & Fee Pipeline: Daily extraction of client records, holdings, fees; joining with Orion data to create client view
- Market Data Pipeline: Daily load of indices, pricing, FX rates from Bloomberg, Refinitiv; joins with portfolio positions for performance analysis
- CRM Pipeline: Daily sync of Salesforce accounts, opportunities, activities; joined with Tamarac for revenue attribution
- Accounting Pipeline: Monthly consolidation of GL entries; joins with Tamarac fee data for revenue recognition and audit trail
paragraphs: Meridian operates a cloud-based data warehouse on Azure Synapse that consolidates data from Orion, Tamarac, Salesforce, accounting systems, and market data feeds. ▌ KEY INSIGHT: The data warehouse is the single source of truth for firm-wide metrics; all dashboards and reports query this system to ensure consistency.

tool:ch9.heading: Chapter 9: Cybersecurity Infrastructure & Data Protection
tool:ch9.raw_text: Meridian Wealth Advisors maintains enterprise-grade cybersecurity and data protection controls aligned with SEC Cybersecurity Guidance, FINRA Rule 4370, and GLBA requirements. The firm operates a Defense-in-Depth strategy with perimeter, endpoint, data, and application-layer security. All security decisions are governed by the Chief Information Security Officer and reviewed quarterly by the Compliance Committee.

PII and regulated data receive highest protection with audit logging at data access point.

tool:ch9:s9.2-9-2-data-classification-an.raw_text:
All firm data is classified into sensitivity tiers that determine handling, access, encryption, and retention. Meridian encrypts sensitive data at rest (AES-256), in transit (TLS 1.2+), and implements key management via Azure Key Vault. PII and regulated data receive highest protection with audit logging at data access point.
Data Classification: PUBLIC; Examples: Marketing materials, published indices; Encryption at Rest: Not required; Encryption in Transit: HTTPS (recommended); Access Controls: No restriction; Retention: Indefinite; Audit Logging: No; Handling Requirements: None
Data Classification: INTERNAL; Examples: Internal memos, org charts, policies; Encryption at Rest: Not required; Encryption in Transit: HTTPS; Access Controls: Domain users; Retention: 7 years; Audit Logging: No; Handling Requirements: Normal backups
Data Classification: CONFIDENTIAL; Examples: Client portfolios, advisor compensation; Encryption at Rest: AES-256 (at rest), TLS 1.2 (transit); Encryption in Transit: TLS 1.2+ mandatory; Access Controls: Role-based + MFA; Retention: 7 years + regulatory; Audit Logging: Full event logging; Handling Requirements: Encryption mandatory, minimal distribution
Data Classification: RESTRICTED; Examples: Client PII, SSN, account numbers, credentials; Encryption at Rest: AES-256 mandatory + HSM key encryption; Encryption in Transit: TLS 1.2+ + Perfect Forward Secrecy; Access Controls: Principle of least privilege + MFA + session recording; Retention: Regulatory period or 7 years; Audit Logging: Full access audit trail; Handling Requirements: Tokenization, minimum field exposure, immediate quarantine on breach

Encryption key management is centralized in Azure Key Vault with automatic rotation on 90-day cycle. All systems that access RESTRICTED data utilize Key Vault for key retrieval; no hardcoded credentials are permitted. Backup encryption keys are stored offline in a secure facility.
paragraphs: All firm data is classified into sensitivity tiers that determine handling, access, encryption, and retention. Meridian encrypts sensitive data at rest (AES-256), in transit (TLS 1.2+), and implements key management via Azure Key Vault. PII and regulated data receive highest protection with audit logging at data access point.

tool:ch11.heading: Chapter 11: Communication, Collaboration & Workflow Systems
tool:ch11.raw_text: Meridian Wealth Advisors operates a unified Microsoft 365 ecosystem for internal communication, collaboration, and workflow automation. All 350+ employees use Microsoft Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint with governance policies that enforce data classification, retention, and access control. The firm also uses Power Automate for business process automation and Calendly for scheduling integration.

Meridian has deployed Microsoft 365 enterprise with full suite of applications: Exchange Online (email/calendar), Teams (chat/meetings), SharePoint (document collaboration), OneDrive (personal file storage), and Office Online (document editing). M365 Service: OneDrive for Business; Configuration Detail: Personal cloud storage (1 TB per user), sync client deployed; Users: 350; Key Governance Policy: Auto-sync to all devices, sharing restricted to internal users only; Data Retention: Recycle bin 93 days; Backup / Redundancy: Microsoft 24-hour protection; Access Control: Individual user control + admin audit

M365 Service: Project for Web; Configuration Detail: Project tracking, Gantt charts, resource management; Users: 28 (Finance + Ops teams); Key Governance Policy: Project templates standardized, time tracking integration; Data Retention: Archive after project close; Backup / Redundancy: Standard SharePoint backup; Access Control: Project-level access control
M365 Service: Power BI Integration; Configuration Detail: Embed dashboards in Teams, share reports via SharePoint; Users: 120 (power users); Key Governance Policy: Premium capacity (P1 license), sensitivity labels applied to datasets; Data Retention: Indefinite; Backup / Redundancy: Separate backup (Synapse); Access Control: App workspace + individual dashboard permissions

tool:ch11:s11.3-11-3-meeting-and-schedul.raw_text:
All meetings are scheduled via Outlook calendar with automatic room booking for conference rooms. Zoom and Teams are available for video conferencing; Teams meetings are preferred for internal calls (recorded by default) while Zoom is used for external vendor calls. Calendly is used for advisor scheduling with clients (limited to 5 calendars for high-volume advisors).
- Outlook Calendar: Enterprise Exchange calendar with 20 conference rooms equipped with video systems (Teams/Zoom), room finder integration, automatic booking
- Teams Meetings: Default for internal meetings, automatic recording to SharePoint, attendance tracking, meeting notes in OneNote integration
- Zoom: Used for external partner/client video calls, encrypted recordings stored in Zoom cloud (90-day retention), screen sharing permitted with host control
- Calendly: Advisor scheduling interface allowing clients to book 30-minute or 1-hour consultation slots; calendar integrated with Outlook; auto-reminders to clients 24 hours and 1 hour before meeting
Scheduling Tool: Outlook Calendar; Primary Use: All internal meetings and room booking; Users: 350; Recording Policy: No recording at calendar level; External Access: External invitees can view free/busy only; Integration Points: Teams meeting auto-join, Zoom link from description; Calendar Capacity: 20 conference rooms
Scheduling Tool: Teams Meetings; Primary Use: Internal meetings, client portals calls; Users: 350; Recording Policy: Auto-record to SharePoint (30-day default); External Access: External guests join via Teams link, no recording; Integration Points: Attendance tracked, OneNote meeting notes; Calendar Capacity: 50 concurrent meetings firm-wide
Scheduling Tool: Zoom; Primary Use: External vendor calls, large webinars; Users: 50 (premium accounts); Recording Policy: Optional recording (encrypted, Zoom cloud); External Access: Host shares link, guest join via browser/app; Integration Points: Zoom native calendar sync (limited); Calendar Capacity: 300 concurrent participants
Scheduling Tool: Calendly; Primary Use: Client appointment scheduling (advisors); Users: 35 high-volume advisors; Recording Policy: No automatic recording; External Access: Public link or embedded on website; Integration Points: Sync to Outlook, SMS reminders via Twilio; Calendar Capacity: Unlimited slots per advisor
Table 11.3: Meeting and Scheduling Platform Architecture
paragraphs: All meetings are scheduled via Outlook calendar with automatic room booking for conference rooms. Zoom and Teams are available for video conferencing; Teams meetings are preferred for internal calls (recorded by default) while Zoom is used for external vendor calls. Calendly is used for advisor scheduling with clients (limited to 5 calendars for high-volume advisors).
Table 11.3: Meeting and Scheduling Platform Architecture

tool:ch12:s12.3-12-3-advisor-compensatio.content_summary:

tool:ch12:s12.4-12-4-performance-trackin.raw_text:
Meridian tracks a comprehensive set of KPIs to monitor firm performance, advisor productivity, and client outcomes. KPIs are reviewed monthly by leadership and quarterly by the Board. Dashboards are built in Power BI with role-based views for different stakeholder groups.
KPI Category: Business Growth; KPI Name: Total AUM; Calculation Method: Orion total portfolio value (EOM); Target / Benchmark: $4.2B (target 12% YoY growth); Reporting Frequency: Monthly; Owner: Chief Operating Officer; Variance Threshold: >5% miss triggers review
KPI Category: Business Growth; KPI Name: Net Revenue; Calculation Method: Total fees less refunds, 12-month rolling; Target / Benchmark: $147M (target 10% growth); Reporting Frequency: Monthly; Owner: Chief Financial Officer; Variance Threshold: >3% variance requires analysis
KPI Category: Business Growth; KPI Name: Net New AUM Flows; Calculation Method: Client deposits minus withdrawals (monthly); Target / Benchmark: $35M/month average; Reporting Frequency: Monthly; Owner: Chief Operating Officer; Variance Threshold: <$25M in quarter triggers review
KPI Category: Advisor Productivity; KPI Name: Average AUM per Advisor; Calculation Method: Total AUM / headcount (advisors only); Target / Benchmark: $60M per advisor (benchmark); Reporting Frequency: Monthly; Owner: Chief Operating Officer; Variance Threshold: <$55M triggers coaching
KPI Category: Advisor Productivity; KPI Name: Fee Production per Advisor; Calculation Method: Total fees / advisor count; Target / Benchmark: $2.0M per advisor (benchmark); Reporting Frequency: Quarterly; Owner: Chief Financial Officer; Variance Threshold: <$1.8M requires discussion
KPI Category: Client Retention; KPI Name: Client Retention Rate; Calculation Method: (Clients EOY / Clients BOY) - Voluntary Closures; Target / Benchmark: >95% (industry benchmark 90%); Reporting Frequency: Quarterly; Owner: Chief Operating Officer; Variance Threshold: <93% escalated to CEO
KPI Category: Client Retention; KPI Name: Revenue Retention; Calculation Method: Retained revenue / prior year revenue; Target / Benchmark: >93% (organic growth metric); Reporting Frequency: Quarterly; Owner: Chief Financial Officer; Variance Threshold: <90% indicates churn risk
KPI Category: Client Satisfaction; KPI Name: Net Promoter Score; Calculation Method: Annual survey, (Promoters - Detractors) / Total; Target / Benchmark: >65 (industry avg 45); Reporting Frequency: Annual; Owner: Chief Marketing Officer; Variance Threshold: <60 triggers strategy review
KPI Category: Risk Management; KPI Name: Portfolio Compliance Rate; Calculation Method: Portfolios meeting IPS guidelines / total portfolios; Target / Benchmark: >98%; Reporting Frequency: Monthly; Owner: Chief Investment Officer; Variance Threshold: <97% requires remediation
KPI Category: Risk Management; KPI Name: Trading Error Rate; Calculation Method: Execution errors / total trades; Target / Benchmark: <0.1% (zero target); Reporting Frequency: Monthly; Owner: Chief Compliance Officer; Variance Threshold: >0.05% escalates to CIO
Table 12.4: Firm KPIs, Calculation Methods, and Performance Thresholds
▌ EXECUTIVE DISCIPLINE: KPIs are reviewed monthly by the Executive Committee with variance analysis and remediation plans; Board receives quarterly summary with trend analysis and outlook.
Additional operational KPIs tracked include compliance violation rate (<2 per quarter), system uptime (>99.5% across mission-critical systems), average response time to client inquiries (<24 hours), and audit findings resolved rate (100% of prior findings closed). Quarterly business reviews include deep dives on underperforming metrics with root cause analysis and corrective action plans.

MuleSoft Anypoint Platform serves as the enterprise integration platform connecting on-premises systems with cloud applications. 15+ integration flows handle real-time and batch data synchronization, transformation, and orchestration. All flows implement error handling, retry logic, and detailed logging.
Integration Flow: Client Sync; Source System: ClientMaster_DB; Target System: CRM (Salesforce); Transformation: JSON mapping; Schedule: Real-time; Error Handling: DLQ + Retry
Integration Flow: Position Feed; Source System: Custodian API; Target System: Portfolio_DB; Transformation: XML→SQL; Schedule: Hourly; Error Handling: Exception queue
Integration Flow: Market Data Ingest; Source System: Bloomberg Terminal; Target System: MarketData_DB; Transformation: FIX→SQL; Schedule: Real-time; Error Handling: Cache fallback
Integration Flow: Transaction Reconcile; Source System: Portfolio_DB; Target System: Billing_DB; Transformation: Dedup & validate; Schedule: Daily EOD; Error Handling: Manual review
Integration Flow: Compliance Check; Source System: Compliance_DB; Target System: Regulatory Portal; Transformation: CSV export; Schedule: Daily; Error Handling: Alert + retry
Integration Flow: Document Index; Source System: DMS (SharePoint); Target System: DocumentMeta_DB; Transformation: Metadata extract; Schedule: Real-time; Error Handling: Archive fallback
Integration Flow: Audit Log Ship; Source System: AuditLog_DB; Target System: SIEM (Splunk); Transformation: Syslog format; Schedule: Real-time; Error Handling: Buffer + batch
Integration Flow: Fee Calculation; Source System: Billing_DB; Target System: Accounting (NetSuite); Transformation: Journal entries; Schedule: Monthly; Error Handling: GL verification
Integration Flow: Performance Report; Source System: Analytics_DW; Target System: Client Portal; Transformation: HTML + PDF; Schedule: Daily; Error Handling: Retry + email
Integration Flow: Model Portfolio Sync; Source System: Planning_DB; Target System: Trading System; Transformation: Rebalance rules; Schedule: Daily; Error Handling: Validation checks
Integration Flow: Tax Reporting; Source System: Portfolio_DB; Target System: Tax Software (UltraTax); Transformation: Tax lots export; Schedule: Annual; Error Handling: Manual QA
Integration Flow: HR System Sync; Source System: HR_DB; Target System: Payroll (ADP); Transformation: Employee record; Schedule: Weekly; Error Handling: Reconciliation

tool:ch15:s15.2-15-2-disaster-recovery-a.heading: 15.2 Disaster Recovery Architecture
tool:ch15:s15.2-15-2-disaster-recovery-a.content_summary:
Meridian operates a geographically distributed disaster recovery infrastructure with primary production datacenter in New York and secondary DR site in New Jersey, 50 miles distant. Critical systems replicate synchronously (RPO=0) while non-critical systems use asynchronous replication.
Primary Production Site (New York): 1,200 sq ft, 15 cabinets, 120 servers, dual power feeds from separate utility substations, 10 Gbps redundant internet connectivity. Secondary DR Site (New Jersey): 800 sq ft, 1…
tool:ch15:s15.2-15-2-disaster-recovery-a.raw_text:
Meridian operates a geographically distributed disaster recovery infrastructure with primary production datacenter in New York and secondary DR site in New Jersey, 50 miles distant. Critical systems replicate synchronously (RPO=0) while non-critical systems use asynchronous replication.
Primary Production Site (New York): 1,200 sq ft, 15 cabinets, 120 servers, dual power feeds from separate utility substations, 10 Gbps redundant internet connectivity. Secondary DR Site (New Jersey): 800 sq ft, 10 cabinets, 80 servers (standby), single power feed, 5 Gbps internet. Quarterly DR tests exercise failover of critical applications with recovery time measurements and post-test validation.
- DR Site Configuration: Active-Passive for databases; synchronous replication using Always-On SQL Server availability groups; warm standby for application servers; automated database failover with <5 minute cutover
- Network Failover: DNS failover configured in Route53; BGP failover for internet connectivity; WAN accelerators cache data at both sites; VPN tunnels maintain active replication tunnels
- Testing Schedule: Quarterly full system recovery tests; monthly isolated component tests; annual full-scale tabletop exercise with business units
paragraphs: Meridian operates a geographically distributed disaster recovery infrastructure with primary production datacenter in New York and secondary DR site in New Jersey, 50 miles distant. Critical systems replicate synchronously (RPO=0) while non-critical systems use asynchronous replication.

Secondary DR Site (New Jersey): 800 sq ft, 10 cabinets, 80 servers (standby), single power feed, 5 Gbps internet. Quarterly DR tests exercise failover of critical applications with recovery time measurements and post-test validation.

tool:ch15:s15.4-15-4-business-continuity.raw_text:
Meridian maintains detailed business continuity procedures for 8 major disaster scenarios. Each procedure includes decision criteria, escalation path, recovery sequence, communication templates, and success criteria. All BC procedures are reviewed and approved annually by Chief Risk Officer.
Disaster Scenario: Primary DC Loss; Trigger Criteria: Multiple system down >5min; Recovery Sequence: 1. Declare DR; 2. Failover DB; 3. Route traffic; 4. Restore apps; Est. Time to Resume: 90 minutes; Key Stakeholders: CRO, CTO, Ops; Comms Plan: SMS + email + calls
Disaster Scenario: Ransomware Attack; Trigger Criteria: Encryption detected; backup queue blocked; Recovery Sequence: 1. Isolate network; 2. Activate backups; 3. Forensics; 4. Restore from safe point; Est. Time to Resume: 4-6 hours; Key Stakeholders: CISO, CTO, Legal; Comms Plan: Exec + staff + clients
Disaster Scenario: Pandemic/Staff Loss; Trigger Criteria: Office closure; key staff unavailable; Recovery Sequence: 1. Activate remote work; 2. Delegate authority; 3. Split responsibilities; 4. Establish hotline; Est. Time to Resume: Immediate; Key Stakeholders: HR, CRO, Ops; Comms Plan: Email + portal
Disaster Scenario: Key Person Loss; Trigger Criteria: Critical staff sudden departure; Recovery Sequence: 1. Cross-train backup assumes role; 2. Legal/HR involvement; 3. Client notification; 4. Knowledge transfer; Est. Time to Resume: 1-2 days; Key Stakeholders: HR, Department head; Comms Plan: Email
Disaster Scenario: Custodian Outage; Trigger Criteria: Unable to connect to custodian API; Recovery Sequence: 1. Use backup data; 2. Contact custodian; 3. Escalate to manager; 4. Client comms; Est. Time to Resume: 2-4 hours; Key Stakeholders: Ops, Portfolio, Client Svc; Comms Plan: Email + portal notice
Disaster Scenario: Internet Outage; Trigger Criteria: No external connectivity; Recovery Sequence: 1. Activate backup WAN; 2. Local processing mode; 3. Batch operations; 4. Resume normal; Est. Time to Resume: 15 minutes to local; 1hr full; Key Stakeholders: CTO, Ops, Vendor; Comms Plan: Internal comms
Disaster Scenario: Power Failure; Trigger Criteria: Multiple systems offline; UPS depleted; Recovery Sequence: 1. Activate battery backup; 2. Start generator; 3. Load balance; 4. Failover if prolonged; Est. Time to Resume: 5 min on battery; 30 min on gen; Key Stakeholders: Facilities, CTO, Ops; Comms Plan: Internal
Disaster Scenario: Regulatory Outage; Trigger Criteria: SEC, FINRA, banking systems down; Recovery Sequence: 1. Continue local processing; 2. Batch filings; 3. Document delays; 4. Notify regulators; Est. Time to Resume: Depends on regulator RTO; Key Stakeholders: Compliance, Legal; Comms Plan: Email to regulators
Table 15.4.1: Disaster Recovery Procedures Matrix
paragraphs: Meridian maintains detailed business continuity procedures for 8 major disaster scenarios. Each procedure includes decision criteria, escalation path, recovery sequence, communication templates, and success criteria. All BC procedures are reviewed and approved annually by Chief Risk Officer.
Table 15.4.1: Disaster Recovery Procedures Matrix

Assessments are scored using a 100-point scale with ratings: 0-40 High Risk (red), 41-70 Medium Risk (yellow), 71-100 Low Risk (green).

Assessment Dimension: Financial Stability; Evaluation Criteria: Credit rating; revenue growth; debt-to-equity; liquidity ratios; audited financials; Data Sources: S&P reports; D&B score; vendor financials; regulatory filings; Frequency: Annual; Passing Score: ≥70 points; Owner: CFO
Assessment Dimension: Operational Resilience; Evaluation Criteria: RTO/RPO SLAs; 24/7 support; incident management; disaster recovery test results; Data Sources: Service agreements; support contracts; DR test docs; uptime reports; Frequency: Annual; Passing Score: ≥75 points; Owner: CRO
Assessment Dimension: Compliance Posture; Evaluation Criteria: Regulatory licenses; audit history; fines/violations; privacy certifications; AML/KYC; Data Sources: Regulatory databases; vendor attestation; EDGAR filings; audit reports; Frequency: Annual; Passing Score: ≥70 points; Owner: CCO
Assessment Dimension: Concentration Risk; Evaluation Criteria: Percentage of AUM with single vendor; alternative vendors available; switching cost; Data Sources: Internal analysis; contract review; vendor benchmark analysis; Frequency: Quarterly; Passing Score: ≤20% AUM; Owner: CRO

Meridian performs quarterly concentration analysis to ensure no single vendor represents >20% of critical operations. Fidelity as primary custodian represents 85% of AUM but contractual language prevents unilateral termination requiring 6-month notice. Charles Schwab maintains 15% as active backup custodian. Cloud infrastructure split between AWS (70%) and Azure (30%) provides provider diversification.
- Custodian Concentration: Fidelity 85%, Charles Schwab 15%; requires 6-month transition if custodian change needed
- Cloud Provider: AWS 70% (data warehouse, APIs, backups), Azure 30% (identity, collaboration); can migrate between clouds in 2-3 weeks
- Market Data: Bloomberg primary; S&P, FactSet as backups; switch cost <1 week, annual cost difference <5%
- CRM: Salesforce; no immediate replacement identified but cost to implement alternative is 4-6 months

tool:ch17.heading: Chapter 17: System Administration, Change Management & SDLC
tool:ch17.content_summary: Chapter 17: System Administration, Change Management & SDLC
tool:ch17.raw_text: Meridian enforces rigorous change management and system development lifecycle (SDLC) processes ensuring all infrastructure changes, security patches, and application enhancements are properly reviewed, tested, approved, and documented. All changes are tracked in ServiceNow with full audit trail for compliance.
tool:ch17.label: Chapter 17: System Administration, Change Management & SDLC

tool:ch17:s17.1-17-1-change-management-p.heading: 17.1 Change Management Process
tool:ch17:s17.1-17-1-change-management-p.content_summary:
All changes are classified into three categories: Standard (pre-approved routine updates), Normal (significant changes requiring CAB approval), and Emergency (urgent changes requiring post-implementation approval). Change Advisory Board meets weekly to review and approve normal changes; emergency changes follow expedited approval process.
Change Type: Standard; Definition: Pre-approved routine updates, patches, small config changes; Examples: Apply OS security patch, rotate backup media, add use…

All changes are classified into three categories: Standard (pre-approved routine updates), Normal (significant changes requiring CAB approval), and Emergency (urgent changes requiring post-implementation approval). Change Advisory Board meets weekly to review and approve normal changes; emergency changes follow expedited approval process.
Change Type: Standard; Definition: Pre-approved routine updates, patches, small config changes; Examples: Apply OS security patch, rotate backup media, add user account; Approval Path: ServiceNow auto-approved if meets criteria; Notification: Stakeholder email; Backout Plan: Required if production; Max Duration: 4 hours
Change Type: Normal; Definition: Moderate risk infrastructure or application changes; Examples: Add database index, update network ACLs, deploy app version; Approval Path: CAB vote (50% quorum); Notification: Change calendar notification; Backout Plan: Mandatory detailed plan; Max Duration: 8 hours
Change Type: Emergency; Definition: Unplanned urgent changes to restore service; Examples: Restore from backup, hotfix security breach, change connectivity; Approval Path: VP on-call verbal approval + email; Notification: Immediate all-hands; Backout Plan: Automatic rollback if available; Max Duration: 2 hours
Change Type: Security; Definition: Urgent security patches, vulnerability remediation; Examples: Apply critical security patch, revoke compromised credentials; Approval Path: CISO approval only; Notification: CISO + affected teams; Backout Plan: Rollback plan required; Max Duration: ASAP

tool:ch17:s17.2-17-2-sdlc-for-custom-dev.content_summary:

tool:ch17:s17.2-17-2-sdlc-for-custom-dev.raw_text:
All custom application development follows a 7-phase SDLC enforced through Jira templates and mandatory approvals at phase gates. Projects are tracked in Jira with automated escalation if phase gates are missed. Code is reviewed peer and security team before production deployment.
Phase: 1. Requirements; Deliverables: Business requirements doc, use cases, acceptance criteria, cost estimate; Tools: Jira, Confluence, Excel; Approval: Product Owner sign-off; Duration: 1-2 weeks; Success Criteria: Signed requirements with test cases
Phase: 2. Design; Deliverables: Architecture diagram, DB schema, API specs, security review, tech debt assessment; Tools: Visio, SQL scripts, Swagger, OWASP review; Approval: Tech Lead + CISO approval; Duration: 1-3 weeks; Success Criteria: Design review passed, security approved
Phase: 3. Development; Deliverables: Code commits with peer review, unit tests, code coverage >80%, documentation; Tools: Git, Jenkins, SonarQube, Jira; Approval: Code review 2+ approvers; Duration: 2-8 weeks; Success Criteria: Code quality gates passed
Phase: 4. Testing; Deliverables: Functional testing plan, regression suite, performance testing, load testing; Tools: TestRail, JMeter, Selenium, LoadRunner; Approval: QA Lead approval; Duration: 1-4 weeks; Success Criteria: All test cases passed, <1% defects
Phase: 5. UAT; Deliverables: User acceptance test plan, business sign-off, training materials, runbooks; Tools: TestRail, UAT environment, video tutorials; Approval: Business Owner acceptance; Duration: 1-2 weeks; Success Criteria: Business sign-off 100% passing
Phase: 6. Deployment; Deliverables: Deployment plan, rollback procedure, change ticket, runbook; Tools: ServiceNow, Infrastructure-as-Code, monitoring; Approval: CAB approval for production; Duration: Project window; Success Criteria: Zero impact to production; monitoring active
Phase: 7. Post-Deploy; Deliverables: Incident review, performance metrics, documentation updates, lessons learned; Tools: Splunk, DataDog, Jira, wiki; Approval: Project Manager/Tech Lead; Duration: 1 week; Success Criteria: All metrics green; incidents resolved
Table 17.2.1: SDLC Phases and Governance

tool:ch17:s17.4-17-4-configuration-manag.raw_text:
Meridian maintains a comprehensive Configuration Management Database (CMDB) in ServiceNow tracking all IT assets including servers, applications, databases, networks, and software licenses. The CMDB is automatically synchronized with AWS and Azure cloud inventories. All configuration items (CIs) require documentation of relationships, dependencies, and change history.
- Server CIs: 180+ servers tracked with OS, CPU, RAM, storage, location, backup status, patch level, owner, cost center
- Application CIs: 45+ applications with version, vendor, license count, renewal date, business owner, business criticality, integration points
- Database CIs: 10 production databases + 8 non-prod with tables, row counts, backup schedule, replication targets, SLA tiers
- Network CIs: Firewalls, routers, switches, WANs documented with capacity, redundancy, failover configuration, IPAM records
- License CIs: 200+ software licenses tracked with expiration, renewal cost, deployment count, vendor contact, true-up audits
paragraphs: Meridian maintains a comprehensive Configuration Management Database (CMDB) in ServiceNow tracking all IT assets including servers, applications, databases, networks, and software licenses. The CMDB is automatically synchronized with AWS and Azure cloud inventories. All configuration items (CIs) require documentation of relationships, dependencies, and change history.
tool:ch17:s17.4-17-4-configuration-manag.label: 17.4 Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

tool:ch18:s18.2-18-2-glossary-of-technic.raw_text:
Comprehensive glossary defining 40+ technical terms, financial concepts, and regulatory acronyms used throughout this knowledge base.
AUM: Assets Under Management - total client assets managed by Meridian
API: Application Programming Interface - standardized method for systems to communicate
RTO: Recovery Time Objective - maximum acceptable time to restore a system after failure
RPO: Recovery Point Objective - maximum acceptable amount of data loss (time since last backup)
SLA: Service Level Agreement - contractual commitment between vendor and customer on performance
MTPD: Mean Time to Perform Duties - average time to restore business processes after failure
CUSIP: Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures - unique security identifier
EOD: End of Day - market closing time (typically 4 PM ET for US markets)
ETL: Extract-Transform-Load - data integration process extracting from sources, transforming, loading to target
ELT: Extract-Load-Transform - alternative approach where transformation occurs post-load in target system
SFTP: SSH File Transfer Protocol - secure method for transferring files over encrypted connection
MFT: Managed File Transfer - enterprise solution for file exchange with encryption and audit logging
DLQ: Dead Letter Queue - queue for messages that cannot be processed normally
SIEM: Security Information and Event Management - platform for log aggregation and security monitoring
SOX: Sarbanes-Oxley - US regulation requiring financial controls and audit trail documentation
KYC: Know Your Customer - regulatory requirement to verify client identity and beneficial ownership
OWASP: Open Web Application Security Project - standards for secure application development
CI/CD: Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment - automated testing and deployment pipeline
IaC: Infrastructure as Code - managing infrastructure through version-controlled code (Terraform, CloudFormation)
HA: High Availability - system design to minimize downtime through redundancy
DR: Disaster Recovery - processes and systems enabling recovery from catastrophic failures
BC: Business Continuity - broader set of procedures ensuring business operations continue during disruptions
DW: Data Warehouse - centralized repository for analytical data (separate from operational databases)
BI: Business Intelligence - analytics, reporting, and visualization of business data
CMDB: Configuration Management Database - repository of all IT assets and their relationships
CAB: Change Advisory Board - governance body reviewing and approving system changes
QA: Quality Assurance - processes and testing to ensure quality of software and systems
UAT: User Acceptance Testing - final testing phase by business users before production deployment
CSS: Cascading Style Sheets - styling markup language for web applications
REST: Representational State Transfer - architectural style for web APIs using HTTP methods
JSON: JavaScript Object Notation - lightweight data interchange format
XML: Extensible Markup Language - markup language for structured data exchange
SWIFT: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication - messaging standard for financial transactions
FIX: Financial Information eXchange - standardized protocol for real-time securities trading
ACH: Automated Clearing House - US system for electronic funds transfers
XBRL: eXtensible Business Reporting Language - standard for financial reporting to regulators
BGP: Border Gateway Protocol - routing protocol directing internet traffic across networks
VPN: Virtual Private Network - encrypted network tunnel for secure remote connectivity
TLS: Transport Layer Security - encryption protocol (replaces SSL) for securing network communications
OAuth: Open Authorization - framework for delegated authentication without sharing passwords
paragraphs: Comprehensive glossary defining 40+ technical terms, financial concepts, and regulatory acronyms used throughout this knowledge base.
AUM: Assets Under Management - total client assets managed by Meridian
API: Application Programming Interface - standardized method for systems to communicate
RTO: Recovery Time Objective - maximum acceptable time to restore a system after failure
RPO: Recovery Point Objective - maximum acceptable amount of data loss (time since last backup)
SLA: Service Level Agreement - contractual commitment between vendor and customer on performance
MTPD: Mean Time to Perform Duties - average time to restore business processes after failure
CUSIP: Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures - unique security identifier
EOD: End of Day - market closing time (typically 4 PM ET for US markets)
ETL: Extract-Transform-Load - data integration process extracting from sources, transforming, loading to target
